1624.title: In Brief
1624.summary: Recent highlights include Didem Öğmen’s Manchet design notes, Microsoft’s Michelangelus typeface, Arsenal’s Rocastle identity, Richard Niessen’s Kanaalpark, and new work on type history, multilingual type, and accessibility. The roundup also covers Tegaki, SuperTipo Veloz, and Depesi poster types.

1623.title: Street Lettering, Manhole Covers and Stone Inscriptions
1623.summary: Jack Usine turns technical imperfections in lettering into an expressive visual language. Other stories look at French sign painting, Persian inscriptions on Iranian cast-iron manhole covers, and a custom stone inscription for The Hague’s Kloosterkerk.

1622.title: Typography in a Multilingual World
1622.summary: Monotype and Canva expand access to typefaces for Arabic, Bengali, Hindi, Khmer, Lao, Thai, and Vietnamese; TypeTogether’s Futura100 now supports 23 scripts. The issue also examines multilingual wayfinding in Indian metro systems, Typoday 2026, and type inspired by Tamil kolam floor art.

1621.title: Responsibility, Ownership and the Measure of Labor
1621.summary: Two Ukrainian speakers withdrew from ATypI 2026 after Alexandra Korolkova was included in the programme, prompting debate about ParaType, typefaces made for Astra Linux, responsibility, and professional platforms. The issue considers how ownership, labor, and political context shape the type industry.

1022.title: In Brief
1022.summary: This roundup features YaziBursa’s archive of local lettering, Ahmet Altun’s Maride typeface, tools for comparing and discovering fonts, and an exploration of left-leaning “retalic” type. It also includes news about Armenian printing in Istanbul.

1021.title: New Directions in Type Design and Promotion
1021.summary: New type releases make their design logic part of the story, from Azimut, a free family created for Strasbourg’s UNESCO World Book Capital programme, to typefaces shaped by place and cultural references. The issue looks at how designers present, distribute, and explain new families.

1020.title: AI, Human Craft and Historical Type
1020.summary: A discussion about AI-generated historical lettering shows how image models can invent inaccurate forms and present fabricated references as authentic. The issue contrasts those limits with archival research and the human craft behind type revivals and historical interpretation.

1019.title: Custom Type as an Identity Tool, from Kits to Official Documents
1019.summary: The 2026 FIFA World Cup typeface raises questions about the balance between brand character and legibility. Other stories examine custom typography for football clubs and uniforms, showing how type can carry identity across sport, institutions, and public communication.

1018.title: In Brief
1018.summary: FontBase’s Fontalog and Font Rankings add visual search and usage rankings, while FontColle offers more detailed filters for Google Fonts. The roundup also covers type education and other tools for discovering and comparing typefaces.

1017.title: From the Street to the Archive: Typographic Sources of Identity
1017.summary: A documentary follows the Noble Signs workshop as it preserves New York’s hand-painted signs. In Lagos, artist Dennis Osadebe turns the city’s hand-painted lettering into monumental steel sculptures, connecting vernacular typography with public art and local identity.

1016.title: Typography’s Historical, Technical and Political Layers
1016.summary: The experimental book New New Typography revisits Jan Tschichold’s principles and asks how they shape design today. Other stories trace typography through its material production, including the tools and working conditions behind typefounding.

1015.title: AI, Consent and the Limits of Production
1015.summary: Type foundries take different positions on AI: Mass Driver rejects its use in design and production, while TypeType argues that distinctive custom type remains important as AI-generated design spreads. The issue explores consent, human labor, and the limits of automated creativity.

1014.title: In Brief
1014.summary: The roundup includes calligraphy exhibitions by Selahattin Ganiz and Merve Ersan, the upcoming Now26 conference in Paris, and new books and events for type designers.

1013.title: Cultural Memory and the Power of Archives
1013.summary: A book about professor İlhami Turan documents 64 years of Turkish graphic design education, printing, and typography. The issue also looks at archival projects in other regions that preserve local lettering and cultural memory.

1012.title: From Aesthetics to Engineering: Typography and Safety
1012.summary: Volvo Centum, developed with Dalton Maag, treats typography as a safety tool as well as a brand asset. Designed for quick reading while driving, the typeface is intended to remain clear across languages, conditions, and speeds.

1011.title: In Brief
1011.summary: ISType’s “Globe” event and Fontstand’s international typography conference bring designers together in Istanbul and Berlin. The roundup also features Zuzana Licko’s nine-weight Modulator and Ga Maamli, inspired by hand-painted street signs in Ghana.

1010.title: Typography’s Memory: Archives, Ideologies and New Visual Identities
1010.summary: The Typography Debate project brings together 20th-century European manifestos and polemics around New Typography. Newly archived Chinese lettering manuals and the Czech government’s Czechia Sans identity show how historical research informs contemporary visual systems.

1009.title: Typography in the Digital Age: Legibility, Security and Systems
1009.summary: Common typefaces such as Arial and Helvetica can make characters difficult to distinguish, creating opportunities for digital scams. Research on visual cognition and tests of confusing glyphs across system fonts point to legibility as an important part of digital security.

1008.title: A Changing Type Market and Debates About Concentration
1008.summary: Sales data suggests a shift away from hobby marketplaces toward professional and direct font sales. The issue discusses subscriptions, custom type commissions, and how independent designers can build sustainable businesses through their own foundries and customer relationships.

1007.title: In Brief
1007.summary: Erik Spiekermann receives the 2026 Gutenberg Prize for his influence on digital typography and type families including FF Meta and ITC Officina. The roundup also covers the Letrástica Type Festival, a Tokyo lettering camp, TypeLab recordings, and new coding fonts.

1006.title: Archives, Street Lettering and the Material History of Type
1006.summary: Ed Ruscha’s photographs of Sunset Boulevard are reread as a history of Los Angeles signs, from neon to hand-painted lettering. Amsterdam Typography and Netherlands Typography document the region’s lettering and make its changing visual culture easier to explore.

1005.title: Labels, AI and Visual Authority
1005.summary: Elizabeth Goodspeed questions how algorithmic aesthetic labels detach images from their historical and social contexts. Naming a visual trend can create cultural authority, while trend forecasting companies and AI tools shape which categories become visible.

1004.title: Platforms, Ownership and the Type Economy
1004.summary: Monotype brings MyFonts discovery into ChatGPT, turning catalogue search into conversational recommendations. The issue asks how recommendation systems influence type selection and visibility, and considers ownership and power in the type industry.

1003.title: Research, History and Identity: Theoretical Foundations of Typography
1003.summary: Typotheque’s research spans public responses to typeface expression, how readers of Urdu, Arabic, and Persian perceive Nastaliq styles, and accessibility preferences in design. The stories show how empirical research can inform type design and visual communication.

1002.title: The Technical and Conceptual Limits of Variable Fonts
1002.summary: Projects discussed for the TDC72 competition use variable fonts to explore movement and expression beyond standard weight, width, and slant axes. Other experiments consider stencil effects, motion, and pattern-based controls.

1001.title: Licensing Complexity and Market Behavior
1001.summary: A Fontstand survey of more than 1,300 respondents finds a strong preference for one-time font purchases over subscriptions, especially for long-term projects. The results also point to confusion around licensing terms and uncertainty about continued access.

1000.title: In Brief
1000.summary: The roundup covers the TDC72 finalists, the restoration of historic ghost signs in Boston, and new type releases including GT Mechanik. It also highlights exhibitions, books, and lettering projects.

999.title: Licensing, Privacy and the Cost of Free
999.summary: Widespread use of free fonts such as Roboto and Open Sans can create a typographic monoculture, while retail typefaces may offer stronger support and language coverage. The issue also revisits licensing and privacy concerns around Google Fonts and external font servers.

998.title: The Material Layers of History
998.summary: Dalton Maag argues that early digitisation stripped some metal typefaces of qualities found in their printed sources. Its Recast Collection returns to archival specimens and drawings, including a variable reinterpretation of Adrian Frutiger’s 1957 neo-grotesque system.

997.title: AI, Surveillance and Typography
997.summary: Hellcare Regular deliberately rejects easy legibility to critique the bureaucracy and inaccessibility of the US healthcare system. Inspired by difficult medical documents and doctors’ handwriting, the project connects typography with surveillance, power, and patient experience.

996.title: In Brief
996.summary: Elliot Jay Stocks’s Fine Specimens presents contemporary type design, while a lecture by Ayşegül İzer explores Ottoman printing houses and shared cultural histories. The roundup also points to ATypI 2026 at Stanford.

995.title: Digital Infrastructure: CSS, Security and Tools
995.summary: The CSS text-wrap: pretty feature can improve paragraph endings, while font-size-adjust helps preserve apparent size across typefaces. A separate study of confusable Unicode characters across system fonts connects typography with digital security.

994.title: Corporate Identity, Context and Type as Expression
994.summary: Snickers Sans and Arla Smile show how custom type can support recognisable identities across products and markets. Their design balances brand character with practical needs such as readability, multilingual use, and consistency at scale.

993.title: Critiquing Revivals: Historical Archives and Vernacular Sources
993.summary: Robin Mientjes argues that type revivals should learn from historical design principles rather than simply copy old forms. The issue also explores John Baskerville’s punches, street lettering archives in India and France, and typefaces inspired by local vernacular sources.

992.title: In Brief
992.summary: The roundup features Slanted Experimental Type 4.0, the Kalemin Yolculuğu exhibition on the history of writing tools, Toronto’s Swash & Serif festival, and TypeParis’s 2027 programme in Menorca.

991.title: Custom Lettering for Identity: Bars, Film Titles, Sign Language and Kits
991.summary: Stories explore hand-made letters for a bar identity, a DeafCity Hub logotype derived from British Sign Language gestures, and custom film-title typography. They also look at type for football kits and Palermo FC’s broader visual identity system.

990.title: From Archive to Matrix, from Stone to Sign
990.summary: The issue connects Jan Tschichold’s newly accessible archive with overlooked Italian modernist typefaces and the physical matrices used for printing. It also examines Dutch type design, Tuscan lettering, and vernacular sign painting across Europe and South America.

989.title: Scale, AI and Variable Fonts
989.summary: Monotype reports a library of more than 400,000 styles across 300 languages, while new work revisits condensed geometric sans serifs. The issue discusses grade axes, Gotham Variable, and how designers balance historical influence, AI tools, and creative authorship.
